answer: Stake-weighted reputation with slashing resists sybils by making each identity costly. An agent must lock a deposit before it can transact, and higher limits require a history of verifiable work, so a comet of new fake accounts cannot instantly enter a trusted haven. Creating many identities multiplies the locked capital at risk, while honest work is slow to accumulate. If an identity cheats, its stake is slashed and its reputation collapses, like a karst cave roof falling when its supports are removed. Forgery thus becomes expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
